sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
The arm is also unclickable. So far, the only thing that reacts to clicks is the ball (run animation, net change zero).
Let me think about this from a completely different angle. What if the game isn't about clicking objects, but about clicking positions, and the ball moves to the clicked position? Let me test: click a position far from the ball, e.g., (55, 20) — the left side of the ball's row. If the ball slides to that position, then the ball is a cursor that moves to the clicked position.
Wait, but when I clicked (55, 36) — the ball's own position — the ball ran along the ruler. Hmm.
Or: what if the game is "click to move the ball one step at a time," and the run animation is the ball moving to the clicked column? I clicked (55,36): the ball's center is 36... and the ball ran to the right edge (43) and came back. That doesn't fit either.
Hmm, let me reconsider the run animation. What if the small ball sprite on the ruler isn't the ball, but a separate "cursor" that runs from the left edge to the right edge of the panel every time you click the ball? Like a "scan line"? And the piece's dip is...
Actually, wait. What if the game is a "catch" game: a small ball (cursor) runs along the bottom of the panel, and the piece falls from above; you have to position the cup under the piece? But the cup doesn't move...
Or, what if the game is "the piece falls, and the ball bounces it"? No, that's not it.
Let me try a completely different approach: click a position on the ball's row but at a different column, and see if the ball moves there. Click (55, 20).

# Arm unclickable. Test: does clicking a position move the ball there? Click left of ball on same row.
res = action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':55,'col':20}])
print("board_changed", res.get('board_changed'), "no_impact", res.get('no_impact'), "reward", res.get('reward'), "done", res.get('done'))
prev = previous_frame.ascii.split('\n'); cur = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
diffs = [(r,c,prev[r][c],cur[r][c]) for r in range(64) for c in range(64) if prev[r][c]!=cur[r][c]]
print("diffs:", len(diffs), diffs[:30])
print("anim", res.get('animation'))

</function>
</tool_call>
